slides.heading: Rectangle Mania
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Rectangle Mania, a very hard graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Count axis-aligned rectangles whose four corners are all in the point set.
Each pair forming a strictly up-right diagonal identifies one rectangle exactly once.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Count axis-aligned rectangles whose four corners are all in the point set. Each pair forming a strictly up-right diagonal identifies one rectangle exactly once.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Two points forming an up-right diagonal define a rectangle if the other two corners exist.
slides.narration: Two points forming an up-right diagonal define a rectangle if the other two corners exist.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Choosing four points is n to the fourth. Using strictly up-right pairs as diagonals counts each rectangle once in quadratic time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each pair up and to the right
slides.narration: Step by step. First, put points in a set. Second, for each pair up and to the right. Third, check the other two corners. Fourth, count.

slides.caption: Bottom-left & top-right as diagonal
slides.narration: Treat each pair where the second is strictly up and right of the first as a diagonal, and check the other corners.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Answer: 6
slides.narration: Each rectangle is counted exactly once this way: 6 in total.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We store points, and for each ordered pair with b up and right of a, count when both other corners exist.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Requiring up-right ordering is what avoids counting each rectangle four times.
